content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions, mechanisms, and their clinical significance. 1. Trazodone: The levels of trazodone may be altered by an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Sulfamethoxazole and Triamterene: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of triamterene through competition for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Conversely, triamterene increases sulfamethoxazole levels via an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 3. Sulfamethoxazole and Trimethoprim: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 4. Sulfamethoxazole and Trimipramine: Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of trimipramine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 5. Valganciclovir and Sulfamethoxazole: Valganciclovir increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 6. Valproic Acid and Sulfamethoxazole: Valproic acid increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 7. Sulfamethoxazole and Verapamil: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of verapamil by competing for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Similarly, trimethoprim increases verapamil levels through the same mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 8. Sulfamethoxazole and Verteporfin: The combination of these drugs increases phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Sulfamethoxazole and Voriconazole: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Voriconazole similarly increases sulfamethoxazole levels. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Willow Bark and Sulfamethoxazole: Willow bark increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 11. Zafirlukast and Sulfamethoxazole: Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 12. Zidovudine and Sulfamethoxazole: Zidovudine increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic synergism. Sulfamethoxazole increases zidovudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Acetazolamide and Trimethoprim: Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Trimethoprim and Aliskiren: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and Alosetron: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Alpelisib and Trimethoprim: Alpelisib decreases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Trimethoprim and Amantadine: Trimethoprim increases amantadine levels by decreasing elimination, potentially impairing renal clearance and leading to higher plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Trimethoprim and Amiloride: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, particularly at high doses, in renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Amiloride and Sulfamethoxazole: Amiloride increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 20. Aminobenzoate Potassium and Sulfamethoxazole: Aminobenzoate potassium decreases the effects of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Sulfamethoxazole and Aminohippurate Sodium: Sulfamethoxazole interferes with the chemical color development of aminohippurate (PAH), which is essential for accurate renal clearance analysis. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Aminolevulinic Acid (Oral) and Sulfamethoxazole: These drugs increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration of other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 23. Aminolevulinic Acid (Topical) and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase each other's photosensitizing effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Amiodarone and Sulfamethoxazole: Amiodarone increases sulfamethoxazole levels by competing for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Amitriptyline and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases amitriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Amobarbital and Sulfamethoxazole: Amobarbital decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Amoxapine and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases amoxapine levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Anastrozole and Trimethoprim: Anastrozole increases trimethoprim levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Sulfamethoxazole and Antithrombin Alfa/III: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Apalutamide and Trimethoprim: Apalutamide decreases trimethoprim levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Sulfamethoxazole and Argatroban: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Sulfamethoxazole and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Aspirin and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs may increase each other's effects through plasma protein binding competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Sulfamethoxazole and Azathioprine: The combination may cause leukopenia due to additive myelosuppression. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Azithromycin and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 36. Trimethoprim and Balsalazide: Trimethoprim decreases balsalazide levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 37. Sulfamethoxazole and BCG Vaccine (Live): Sulfamethoxazole decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration and wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 38. Sulfamethoxazole and Bemiparin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Trimethoprim and Benazepril: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Sulfamethoxazole and Biotin: Sulfamethoxazole decreases biotin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 41. Sulfamethoxazole and Bivalirudin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Sulfamethoxazole and Bosentan: Sulfamethoxazole increases bosentan levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Bumetanide and Sulfamethoxazole: Bumetanide increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Butabarbital and Sulfamethoxazole: Butabarbital decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Trimethoprim and Canagliflozin: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Trimethoprim and Candesartan: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Cannabidiol and Trimethoprim: Cannabidiol increases trimethoprim levels by decreasing metabolism, potentially inhibiting CYP2C9 activity. Consider dose reduction and monitor closely. 48. Trimethoprim and Captopril: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Carbamazepine and Sulfamethoxazole: Carbamazepine decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and Carvedilol: Sulfamethoxazole increases carvedilol levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Sulfamethoxazole and Celecoxib: Sulfamethoxazole increases celecoxib levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Chlorothiazide and Sulfamethoxazole: Chlorothiazide increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 53. Chlorpromazine and Sulfamethoxazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 54. Chlorthalidone and Sulfamethoxazole: Chlorthalidone increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Trimethoprim and Cholera Vaccine: Trimethoprim decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics. 56. Choline Magnesium Trisalicylate and Sulfamethoxazole: Choline magnesium trisalicylate increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Cimetidine and Sulfamethoxazole: Cimetidine increases sulfamethoxazole levels by competing for renal tubular clearance of basic (cationic) drugs. Monitor closely.
